Code (normalise.py / heating.py): the product-out LHV-to-HHV factor (heating-value-stream product-out cf-hhv-lhv-hydrogen) is applied to rows whose denominator is a MASS or VOLUME of hydrogen already converted to GJ HHV by cf-h2-hhv-mass or cf-h2-hhv-volume, so those values are divided by 1.183 a second time. Examples: electrolyzer_solid-oxide DEA 40 kWh/kg reads 0.859 GJ/GJ instead of 1.016; electrolyzer_low-temperature 55 kWh/kg reads 1.18 instead of 1.40 (about 40 rows); nrel_2009_001-0074/-0085 and nrel_2018_003-0023 on gasifier_coal-petroleum-coke_ccs-concentrated read 0.36-0.70 instead of 0.53-1.01 against the same 271 MJ/kg on the host (1.01); nrel_2009_001-0118 on steam-reformer_methane_ccs-concentrated. Apply product-out only to efficiencies and per-GJ-of-product rows. Then add product-out cf-hhv-lhv-hydrogen to gasifier_biomass-waste, gasifier_coal-petroleum-coke, steam-reformer_methane, autothermal-reformer_hydrogen and reactor_methane-pyrolysis in heating-value-stream.csv: their LHV efficiencies now convert the fuel only (NREL 46.1% LHV reads 43.8% HHV; it should be about 51.8%), so host and capture variants sit on different bases. Do the two together, or the per-kg energy rows on those hosts break the same way.

Code (feedstock.py): a feed-inclusive energy row given only as a range (value-norm blank) escapes the feedstock rule, because the test reads value-norm only. steam-reformer_methane keeps tp-tijani_2022_001-0031 (1.07-1.20 GJ/GJ gross) as its total band high and barthe 0090 (net, excluded above). Test the midpoint of min and max when there is no central.

Raw extraction (midden-extract.py): MIDDEN cards print their energy inputs by carrier but the extraction writes only the sum. TC0357 ATR (natural gas 164, electricity 4.7, heat 42.6 GJ/t; the LHV factor is now applied to the whole 211.3, electricity and heat included), TC0359 biomass gasification (electricity 11.2 only), and TC0360 methane pyrolysis (natural gas 280) should each give carrier rows, so the carriers step uses the card's own split. Today the pyrolysis total (all gas on the card) is split 54/46 between natural gas and electricity using the NREL 2026 electric-heated case.

Methane pyrolysis: nrel_2026_001's reactor_methane-pyrolysis rows (-0120 to -0128, capex, O&M, energy) carry the sheet flag 'PRELIMINARY VALUES, do not use or cite until finalized (I15)'; the modeller should decide whether to set the example aside. The feedstock rule leaves the solid carbon's energy (about 0.55 GJ/GJ) in the SEC by design (feedstock.csv note); the carbon is then priced as gas burned with no co-product credit. Record carbon as a secondary product or an output flow so the levelized cost incl. energy can credit it.

Hydrogen feedstock rule check: SMR (feed-net natural gas 0.62 GJ/GJ, efficiency 64.8%), ATR (0.65 total, 72%), coal gasifier (0.75, 58.9%) and methane pyrolysis (1.19, efficiency 60% from a sibling) read sensibly once the fixes above land; the biomass gasifier's feed (0.80-0.89 GJ/GJ net on the NREL rows) is right on the examples but was scaled to MIDDEN's electricity-only total (fixed above by excluding -0879). Gasifier efficiencies and the per-kg SEC still differ by the LHV issue in the first MANUAL row.

Turboexpander: SEC total 1.04167 is 100/96% from the expander-generator efficiency, an identity that does not describe the line-preheat gas; once the carriers list names natural gas, consider blocking id-sec-from-efficiency on pressure let-down so the total is the preheat duty (hedman_2008_001 1.17).
